rules.source: Ley 19.628 sobre Protección de la Vida Privada — https://www.bcn.cl/leychile/navegar?idNorma=141599
rules.retrieved_snippet: Regulates the treatment of personal data in registries or databases by public organisms or private parties. Promulgated 1999-08-18.

rules.source: Ley 21.719 (reforma de protección de datos personales) — https://www.bcn.cl/leychile/navegar?idNorma=1209272
rules.retrieved_snippet: Under Ley 21.719, personal data of children (under 14) and adolescents (14-18) receives reinforced protection: the minor's own consent is insufficient, verifiable parental/guardian authorization is required, treatment must follow the best-interest-of-the-child principle, and such data is classified as sensitive data. Published 2024-12-13, full force 2026-12-01.

rules.source: Senado de Chile — Redes sociales: datos personales de menores de 14 años deberán contar con autorización de sus padres — https://www.senado.cl/comunicaciones/noticias/redes-sociales-datos-personales-de-menores-de-14-anos-deberan-contar-con
rules.retrieved_snippet: Under Ley 21.719, social media processing of personal data belonging to children under 14 requires parental authorization; data may only be used for the minor's benefit, never for commercial/advertising purposes.

rules.source: Ley 19.496 sobre Protección de los Derechos de los Consumidores — https://www.bcn.cl/leychile/navegar?idNorma=61438
rules.retrieved_snippet: Regulates relations between providers and consumers, establishes consumer-prejudicial infractions and applicable procedures; enforced by SERNAC (Servicio Nacional del Consumidor).

rules.source: No enacted AI-specific statute as of September 2026 — the 'Proyecto de Ley que regula los Sistemas de Inteligencia Artificial' was approved by the Chamber of Deputies on 13 October 2025 and sent to the Senate for review, not yet enacted. Real, already-enacted, AI-adjacent law: Ley No. 21.663 (2024), the Framework Law on Cybersecurity, establishing the National Cybersecurity Agency (ANCI) and security obligations for 'Operators of Vital Importance' using AI in critical infrastructure. — https://regulations.ai/regulations/RAI-CL-NA-SUMMARY-2026
rules.retrieved_snippet: Chile's dedicated AI bill (EU-AI-Act-style risk categories: prohibited/high-risk/limited/minimal) passed the Chamber of Deputies October 2025 and awaits Senate review — not yet law as of this research.

rules.source: Ley 20.422 (2010), Establece Normas sobre Igualdad de Oportunidades e Inclusión Social de Personas con Discapacidad + Decreto Supremo No. 1 (2015) — https://www.bcn.cl/leychile/Consulta/listado_n_sel?comp=&agr=2&_grupo_aporte=&sub=1117
rules.retrieved_snippet: Ley 20.422 (informed by Chile's 2008 ratification of the UN Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities) establishes equal-opportunity/inclusion norms; Supreme Decree No. 1 (2015) requires STATE organisms specifically to implement web accessibility standards. There is currently no legal requirement for private-sector websites — private-sector web accessibility remains voluntary in Chile as of this research, an honest gap, not a citable private-sector obligation.

rules.source: Ley 21.459 (20-06-2022), establece normas sobre delitos informáticos, deroga la Ley 19.223 — https://www.bcn.cl/leychile/navegar?idNorma=1177743
rules.retrieved_snippet: Establishes computer-crime offenses, repeals Ley 19.223 and adapts Chilean law to the Budapest Convention on Cybercrime (promulgated by Decreto 83 of 2017); offenses include improper access to computer systems, capture of data via electromagnetic emissions and harmful alteration or deletion of data.

rules.source: Ley 17.336 sobre Propiedad Intelectual (latest consolidated version 03-NOV-2017, last modified by Ley 21.045; reglamento Decreto 277) — https://www.bcn.cl/leychile/navegar?idNorma=28933
rules.retrieved_snippet: BCN LeyChile lists the consolidated text of Ley 17.336 on intellectual property, last modified by Ley 21.045 (version 03-NOV-2017), with seven pending bills including one on technological protection measures; later amendments include Ley 18.957 (computer programs) and Ley 20.435 (limitations and exceptions).

rules.source: Ley 19.913 (Diario Oficial 18-12-2003), crea la Unidad de Análisis Financiero y modifica disposiciones en materia de lavado y blanqueo de activos — https://www.bcn.cl/leychile/navegar?idNorma=219119
rules.retrieved_snippet: Creates the Unidad de Análisis Financiero (UAF) to prevent the financial system and other economic sectors being used to commit the offenses it describes; art. 3 identifies obligated entities that must file suspicious-operation reports, art. 4 requires declaring cash entering or leaving the country above US$10,000, art. 27 lists predicate offenses; BCN shows the consolidated text last modified by Ley 21.821 (30-MAY-2026).

rules.source: Ley 20.609 (Ley Zamudio), establece medidas contra la discriminación — https://www.bcn.cl/api-leyfacil/servicio/ObtenerGuiaPublicadaHTML?uri=ley-de-no-discriminacion
rules.retrieved_snippet: Creates a judicial mechanism to correct acts of arbitrary discrimination, obliges state bodies to design anti-discrimination policies, sets a special procedure against discriminatory acts by state agents and a penal aggravating circumstance for hate-motivated crimes (per BCN's citizen guide and parliamentary advisory summary); a BCN June 2025 report says a reform bill (Boletín 12748-17) was in a mixed commission — current status not verified.
